pharm: Mixture of porcine-derived lipases, proteases, and amylases that replace deficient endogenous pancreatic enzymes
quick: Start ~500 lipase units/kg per meal; titrate to symptoms (do not exceed 2,500 lipase units/kg/meal)
Take with every meal and snack
Use only if clearly needed; minimal systemic absorption
Weight, growth, nutritional status, steatorrhea, signs of fibrosing colonopathy
summary: Pancrelipase (pancreatin) is a pancreatic enzyme replacement product containing lipases, proteases, and amylases. It is indicated for the treatment of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, such as in cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis, pancreatectomy, or pancreatic cancer. Dosing is based on lipase units and individualized to the patient's symptoms, degree of steatorrhea, and dietary fat. Doses must be capped to avoid fibrosing colonopathy.
indications: Treatment of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency in adult and pediatric patients (e.g., due to cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic surgery, or other causes)

dosage.d: Initial 500 lipase units/kg per meal; titrate to clinical response; do not exceed 2,500 lipase units/kg/meal, 10,000 lipase units/kg/day, or 4,000 lipase units/g dietary fat/day
dosage.t: With each meal; give about half the meal dose with each snack
dosage.n: Total daily dose should reflect about 3 meals plus 2-3 snacks

dosage.d: Approximately 3,000 lipase units per 120 mL of formula or per breastfeeding
dosage.t: With each feeding; mix contents with soft acidic food, do not crush
dosage.n: Do not exceed recommended limits; titrate to growth and stools

dosage.d: Individualize by grams of fat ingested, within the maximum of 4,000 lipase units per gram of fat per day
dosage.n: Used as an alternative to weight-based dosing

admin: Take with every meal and snack and with enough fluid to swallow completely
Do not crush or chew the capsule contents or hold in the mouth (mucosal irritation)
Capsules may be opened and contents mixed with a small amount of soft acidic food (pH 4.5 or less, e.g., applesauce) and taken immediately
Do not mix directly with formula or breast milk that would dissolve the enteric coating
Do not substitute one pancreatic enzyme product for another without dose verification; titrate to clinical symptoms and stool fat
moa: Pancreatic enzyme products contain a mixture of lipases, proteases, and amylases. In the duodenum and proximal small intestine they catalyze hydrolysis of fats to monoglycerides, glycerol, and free fatty acids; proteins to peptides and amino acids; and starches to dextrins and short-chain sugars. They thereby act like the digestive enzyme physiologically secreted by the pancreas, improving nutrient absorption in pancreatic insufficiency.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to the product (porcine-derived); none listed as absolute in current labeling
relative: History of fibrosing colonopathy or high-dose enzyme use
Acute pancreatitis or acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis (caution)
Gout, hyperuricemia, or renal impairment (enzymes may raise uric acid)
monitor: Growth and nutritional status in children
Symptoms of fibrosing colonopathy (abdominal symptoms, bloody stools, obstruction)
Signs of irritation of oral mucosa

preg: Systemic absorption of pancreatic enzymes is minimal, so fetal exposure is not expected. Available data do not indicate a drug-associated risk. Use during pregnancy if clearly needed to maintain maternal nutrition.
lact: Because pancreatic enzymes are minimally absorbed systemically, breastfeeding is not expected to result in exposure of the infant. Pancrelipase may be used during breastfeeding when needed.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment because the enzymes are minimally absorbed. High doses can increase uric acid; use caution in patients with hyperuricemia, gout, or renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment because of minimal systemic absorption.

moderate: May reduce the absorption of folic acid
minor: Acarbose and miglitol (theoretical reduction of effect)
interactions.food: Always take with food (meals and snacks); enteric-coated products should not be mixed with foods of pH above 4.5 that dissolve the coating
interactions.diagnostics: High doses may increase serum and urinary uric acid

serious: Fibrosing colonopathy (with chronic high doses, especially in cystic fibrosis)
emergency: Severe abdominal pain, bloody stools, or signs of bowel obstruction - seek emergency care
Severe allergic reaction with difficulty breathing, hives, or swelling - emergency care

monitoring: Body weight, growth, and nutritional status
Symptoms suggesting fibrosing colonopathy or bowel obstruction
Serum uric acid in patients with gout or hyperuricemia
Adherence to dosing limits (lipase units per kg per meal and per day)
counsel: Take with every meal and snack to help digest food and absorb nutrients
Swallow capsules whole; if unable, open and sprinkle the beads on a small amount of soft acidic food like applesauce and take right away
Do not crush, chew, or hold the beads in your mouth - this can irritate your mouth
Do not change brands or doses without your doctor's advice
Report severe stomach pain, bloody stools, joint pain, or signs of an allergic reaction
pk: Acts locally in the gut during the meal; effect with each dose
Not applicable; enzymes act locally and are not meaningfully absorbed
Acts during the meal; redosed with each meal and snack
Store at 25 C (77 F) with excursions 15-30 C; protect from moisture and heat; keep bottle tightly closed
pearls: Dose in lipase units; do not exceed 2,500 lipase units/kg/meal, 10,000 lipase units/kg/day, or 4,000 lipase units per gram of dietary fat per day (fibrosing colonopathy risk)
Always give with food; enteric coating protects enzymes from gastric acid
Do not crush or chew beads, and do not mix with high-pH foods that dissolve the coating
Pancreatic enzyme products are not interchangeable - re-titrate when switching
Porcine-derived; use caution with pork protein allergy
missed: Take the missed dose with your next meal or snack. Do not take a dose without food, and do not double the dose. Pancreatic enzymes only work when taken with food.
overdose: Chronic high doses are associated with fibrosing colonopathy and hyperuricemia. Acute overdose is generally managed with supportive care and discontinuation. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
